reviews.review: Great game, however after playing over 25 hours with only minor Origin related issues (as origin is required to play ME3). The game will no longer launch due to an issue with Origin after an Origin update. This issue has lasted months with no attempt to resolve it by EA. As this is likely an issue with the Steam version of the game just buy ME3 on Origin and buy ME1 & ME2 on Steam as they do not require the dumpster fire that is Origin to run.
Mass Effect 3 is as fun today as when I first played it when it launched.

I love the series, I love the game- and I absolutely do not recommend anyone buy this.

20+ hours in to the game, running all sorts of side quests and getting really engaged with the story, the game absolutely barfs and dies and WILL NOT START. This is a known, constant problem that's been reported for over 5 years. Suggestions on forums involve running diagnostics and manually clearing the Origin cache- look, the game's old enough to be stable, and it's not, and when it stops it stops hard and you need to spend considerable effort making the game work. And even if you put that effort in, it might not pay off.

Disregard my hours on here I've also played this game probably a dozen times on PS3. It's honestly a shame Mass Effect 3 launched the way it did. With all the DLC out and years of hindsight I'd say the bad rap it STILL gets to this day is completely undeserved. The combat is a LOT more fun compared to ME2 and ME1, it's fast paced and frantic while still strategic with squadmates. There is very stupid stuff that happens in this game, mostly from a robotic ninja dude named Kai Leng and forced dream sequences of a kid, but there are also moments of immense payoff that cannot be compared to any other game series to this day. The dialogue is mostly limited to two choices but this game by far has the best banter out of any game in the entire series Andromeda included. The Citadel DLC alone should redeem this game to any so called fan of the series, but others like Leviathan and From Ashes add a ton to the lore too and properly give context to the ending that at launch admittedly kind of came out of nowhere. Could it have been built up to more naturally and without DLC? Sure. But the setup is there now and no other developer has even attempted something as ambitious as the Mass Effect Trilogy since its completion. I'd honestly go so far to say this is a better game overall than Mass Effect 2 and, while never reaching the story heights of the first game, is a fantastic conclusion to the series and one of the best games of the Seventh Generation of consoles.

A very story focused rendition of Mass Effect. A remarkably mediocre ending, yet satisfying enough to justify closing out a series, and replayable enough to hold it's pricepoint. 
3/5 I would recommend playing it to finish out the original trilogy.

Now the review: 

TLWR: gameplay is great, story is mostly great, sidequests are not as grindy as previous games, cutscenes can get a tad long, DLC is available through Steam, Visual mods are good.

This game is fantastic. The ending of the game leaves a bit to be desired but it does it's job so don't let that be the deciding factor for you.

combat:
-Of the 3 ME games this one has the best gunplay of the 3 ME games
-The melee is actually pretty solid
-Abilities are less impactful if you aren't spec'd as an ability user. Which means if you make the investment for them you lose out on passives but that abilities feel very satisfying.
-Hitboxes can be a bit annoying. it's not gamebreaking but some crates/walls are a little bigger than they look and some enemy images are not able to be hit. It is not bad but there are some times where you may say "That should have hit."

Story:
One of the highest praises I can give for any game is "you will cry." This game makes you so emotionally invested in all the supporting characters which gives you an incredible amount of immersion. With the extended cut dlc (included in all copies now) you will feel satisfied finishing this game.

Gameplay/sidequests:
-Sidequests are not a horrible grind. some feel a bit "meh" as they are text boxes with "yes or no" options at the end but they never made me feel like I was bored with doing them.
-Invisible walls are a thing, you can get softlocked and be unable to get out. Quiting out solves it and, as far as I have found, you are not perma-locked. Sucks but not irredeemable.
-This game has THE MOST cutscenes in the entire series. Sometimes it does drag on a bit.
-There is no secondary vehicle BS, no tin-can hovercar or tank Mako. If you like those vehicles, good for you. I am glad they are gone.

Other things:
-The steam version being attached to the origin store is annoying as you will need to connect to it every time you load the game. 
-Positive: DLC is downloadable and instalable THROUGH STEAM as opposed to me2.
-The Alot mod in combination with Extended Galaxy mod make the game look less dated and have better UI while not changing ANYTHING from the story making them good mods to add for the vanilla base-game.

Non-Vanilla Mods:
-These mods are very hit and miss as some have sub-par voice acting/animations but use at your own discretion. 
-Romance mods typically are done pretty well, if you are 18+ and intend on romancing Tali I do very much suggest getting hers.
Not as good as ME2, but it's good!
